section_summary.extract_value: This section details a principal components analysis (PCA) conducted on 10 Creativity Achievement Questionnaire (CAQ) domain scores from 847 participants. The analysis explored both a three-factor solution, interpreted as "expressive," "performance," and "scientific" achievement, and a forced two-factor solution, which yielded the standard "Arts" and "Science" dichotomy. The text references Table 4 and Table 5 for factor loadings, but these tables were not provided.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the results of a principal components analysis performed on the 10 CAQ domain scores of 847 participants. It describes a three-factor solution, interpreted as "expressive," "performance," and "scientific" achievement, and a forced two-factor solution, interpreted as "Arts" and "Science." Table 4 presents the CAQ domains and their loadings on the three derived factors.
section_summary.evidence_source: The 10 CAQ domain scores of the 847 participants were subjected to a principal components analysis, with varimax rotation. The initial principal components analysis of the 10 CAQ domains yielded a four-factor solution as the best fit for the data, accounting for 54.3% of the variance. However, a three-factor solution, accounting for 43.8% of the variance, was indicated by the scree plot, and appeared more easily interpretable after varimax rotation. [...] Table 4 presents the CAQ domains and their loadings on the three derived factors. [...] we decided to force a two-factor solution to see if it would yield the standard arts/science dichotomy. [...] Factor 1 included drama, humor, music, visual arts, and creative writing and was interpreted as "Arts." Factor 2 included invention, scientific discovery, and culinary arts and was interpreted as "Science."
